source.basis: Operator spec page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
CyrusOne's NVA9 campus in Sterling, Virginia publishes 38 MW of IT capacity and 700,000 square feet of technical space, and ranks 16th among the 29 Virginia facilities that publish a megawatt figure.

The pattern here is a facility with a large published power envelope and no published rack or accelerator count. At 40 kW per rack, a common AI training density, 38 MW is roughly 950 racks. At 10 kW per rack it is roughly 3,800. The megawatt figure is the operator's, the rack count is an assumption, and the two should not be quoted as the same thing.

Virginia is the largest state on this site's map by a wide margin, with 376 mapped facilities and 2,563.4 MW of published capacity across 29 facilities that publish a figure. NVA9 sits in the top tier of that published capacity. But most mapped Virginia sites publish no megawatt figure at all, so the 2,563.4 MW total is a floor rather than a full accounting of what the state has built.

No certifications are listed for this campus. The spec page does not state whether the site is qualified for federal, financial, or health-data workloads, and it does not state which tenants occupy it. The certification field should be read as empty rather than as a claim about what the campus can host.

suitability.basis: weighted mean of the published inputs named here, scaled to 100; formula on the methodology page
